The Earth's 1st artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, is launched on a Soviet R-7 rocket. October 4, 1957

Sputnik 1 was a 58 cm (23 in) diameter polished metal sphere, with four external radio antennas to broadcast radio pulses. This surprise 1957 success precipitated triggered the Space Race, a part of the larger Cold War. The launch ushered in new political, military, technological, and scientific developments. Every 96.2 minutes for the next 3 months, the satellite made an orbit. It traveled at approximately 18,000 mph in highly elliptical, low Earth orbit. Sputnik provided scientists with valuable information about the density of the upper atmosphere from the drag in its orbit and the propagation of its radio signals gave information about the ionosphere. The radio signals, which were detectable worldwide even by amateur radio operators, continued for 21 days until the transmitter batteries ran out. Sputnik 1 burned up on 4 January 1958 upon reentering Earth's atmosphere, after travelling about 70 million km (43.5 million miles).
